answer: Tie each agent to a TPM-bound identity card: the chip inside its host signs every action, and the network trusts each card only once per device. First, the agent proves its chip fingerprint to a registry. Second, it posts a $200 bond tied to that fingerprint. Third, peers check the fingerprint before accepting work. Fourth, misbehavior burns the bond and revokes the card. Forging 10,000 fake agents then needs 10,000 machines, $2,000,000 in bonds, and 45 days of checks. Like a pearl forming around one grain of sand, trust on the terrace grows one verified vertex at a time. - Jowy
